title: 66 Four-day teacher professional development increases agricultural literacy awareness, tackles food science and poultry science misconceptions
content:
Abstract
After hosting a successful USDA/NIFA funded agricultural literacy professional development (ACRE), Mississippi teachers wanted to engage in more professional development around animal agriculture. Food science and poultry science are topics teachers teach to expose their students to other agricultural areas. Therefore, the Agricultural Science Professional Development 2.0 (ACRE 2.0) Project addresses Mississippi’s top commodity--poultry/eggs-$3.25 billion in 2023 (Mississippi Department of Agriculture and Commerce, 2024) and other food commodities. Teachers were afforded the opportunity to participate in a 4-day summer institute focusing on poultry and food science, literacy instruction, and socio-emotional learning. The objective was to improve the quality of education for Mississippi K-12 students by advancing teachers’ understanding and practices of agricultural literacy related to food science and poultry science. Teachers (cohort 1, n = 28; cohort 2, n = 26), who participated received continuing education credits (CEU’s) for recertification of their teaching license, a stipend, and classroom materials. They learned agriculture content, engaged in hands-on learning labs (e.g. sensory evaluation, embryo development, agar plates/swabbing, food preservation), participated in field excursions (e.g. poultry research unit tour), received literary strategy instruction, and discussed socio-emotional learning in relation to hunger in Mississippi. Program outcomes were achieved by teachers completing surveys (n = 2), interviews (n = 2), and lesson plan submissions (n = 2). Qualitative coding was applied to the data. Teachers post-interview and post-survey data indicated they have a deeper understanding of what it means to be agriculturally literate than they did prior to the institute. For example, teachers spoke of the interconnectedness of agriculture and the environment in the post interview data. Teacher 420 said, “agricultural literacy refers to understanding the interconnected systems of agriculture, including food production, environmental sustainability, economics, and societal impacts. It means being knowledgeable about where our food comes from, how it’s grown or raised, and the broader implications for our health and the environment.” Prior to the institute, many of the teachers provided a simpler definition of what it meant to be agriculturally literate. This institute addressed and corrected many common food science and poultry science misconceptions. One misconception addressed was that chickens are given hormones and steroids to make them grow bigger and faster; pre-survey 40 teachers answered true, post-survey 53 teachers refuted that statement. Teacher 424 noted, “This statement is absolutely false. Their growth has changed since the 1950’s due to the expertise of our scientists and the research they have done to improve genetics, safe food, and better environment for growth.” As such, ACRE 2.0 achieved project goals of increasing teacher understanding of food and poultry science and agricultural literacy practices. Funding provided by the USDA/NIFA National Institute of Food and Agriculture, AFRI Agricultural Workforce Training Priority Area, award # 2022-08873.
